non-goals.item: Adopting a named scaling framework wholesale [E-23]

primary-risks.risk: Scaling adds communication paths (N(N-1)/2) faster than capability
Team structure misaligned with desired architecture

context-assessment.uncertainty: Scaling paths are context-dependent. Framework label is not the dominant predictor; execution context matters.
context-assessment.dependency-density: Multi-team work multiplies dependency surfaces. Conway's Law is a force of nature, not advice.

primary.rationale: Scaling framework choice has negligible practical effect size. Local context, experience, and execution quality dominate.
primary.team-level: Each team chooses cadence (Scrum) or flow (Kanban) based on their work arrival mode and preference.
primary.cross-team: Lightweight alignment through shared outcomes (OKR-like), dependency management, and integration cadence.
primary.governance: Quarterly/half-year outcomes to align. Execution stays at team level through WIP limits and small increments.

scaling-framework-guidance.principle: Scaling frameworks are most useful when they standardize interfaces and decision rights, create reusable patterns for multi-team cadence, and reduce coupling through architecture investment.
scaling-framework-guidance.warning: Empirical comparisons suggest scaling brand choice has negligible practical effect size. Tailor locally rather than adopting wholesale.

anti-patterns.item: Framework orthodoxy: do not adopt SAFe/LeSS/Scrum-of-Scrums wholesale. Tailoring matters more than brand.
Meeting overload: scaling multiplies rituals. Each meeting must demonstrably improve coordination or be eliminated.
Leadership disengagement: only 15% of leaders actively participate — this is the top failure predictor. Leaders must engage.

conways-law.principle: Organization structure will mirror in architecture. Design teams to promote the desired architecture (Inverse Conway Maneuver).
conways-law.assessment: Map current team structure against desired system architecture. Identify misalignments.

communication-paths.warning: Communication paths: N(N-1)/2. 6 people = 15 paths, 10 people = 45 paths, 20 people = 190 paths. Keep teams small.
communication-paths.max-team-size: Teams above 9 are 3-4x more expensive with 2-3x more defects.

alignment-mechanisms.mechanism: Teams align to outcomes, not tasks. Each team owns their decomposition.
Cross-team dependency map review. Focus on reducing, not just tracking.
All teams merge to shared trunk daily. CI validates cross-team integration.

strategy.principle: Eliminate dependencies before tracking them. Architecture investment is cheaper than coordination overhead.

actions.action: Modular boundaries with stable API contracts between teams
Platform team absorbs shared infrastructure dependencies
Enabling teams temporarily coach capability gaps instead of creating permanent dependencies

estimation.approach: Each team forecasts from their own throughput data. Program-level forecast aggregates with dependency risk buffer.
estimation.buffer: Add 15-25% coordination buffer per additional team involved in a shared outcome.

phase.name: assess-and-design
phase.goal: Map current state. Identify Conway's Law misalignments. Design target team topology. Define interaction modes.

phase.name: seed-teams
phase.goal: Form teams. Establish team-level delivery practices. Set up cross-team integration.

phase.name: establish-flow
phase.goal: Teams delivering autonomously. Cross-team dependencies actively reduced. Flow metrics trending positive.

phase.name: optimize
phase.goal: Continuous topology evolution. Dependency reduction. Measurement-driven improvement.
